reports.title: AMD Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

lines: For the fourth quarter of 2026, AMD expects revenue to be approximately $17 billion, plus or minus 3%.

desk.headline: Revenue up 45% to a record $13.4bn, beat; Q4 outlook of ~$17bn well above estimates
results: Record quarter: revenue rose 45% to $13.4bn, above the top of AMD's own guidance; adjusted EPS rose 74% to $2.09.
Data Center nearly doubled to $8.5bn on EPYC server chips and the launch of Instinct MI450 GPUs; its operating income rose to $2.9bn.
Client and Gaming fell 8% to $3.7bn: PC chips grew 7% to $2.9bn but gaming dropped 40% to $773m. Embedded rose 29% to $1.1bn.
GAAP EPS of $1.46 was held back by a $1.1bn charge for the changing value of warrants issued to customers.
Free cash flow fell to $554m as inventory rose to $11.5bn; debt rose to $7.1bn after a $4.75bn bond issue in August.

guidance.summary: AMD expects Q4 revenue of about $17bn (plus or minus 3%), up about 66% on a year ago and 27% on Q3, with non-GAAP gross margin of about 55%.

points: CEO Lisa Su expects growth to speed up further in Q4 as production of Helios racks and 'Venice' server chips ramps.
Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle are among the first customers running workloads on Helios rack systems.
As reported, one large AI lab plans to use up to 2 GW of MI450 chips, with the first big phase due in the first half of 2027.
AMD agreed to buy World Labs and Taalas (inference chips); both deals are expected to close by end-2026.
Management is confident it can sustain very strong growth and expanding profits over the coming years.
call.source: Management comments in the press release (Exhibit 99.1) and earnings slides (Exhibit 99.2), plus XTB, 3 Nov 2026; no call transcript found

watch: Whether Helios and MI450 shipments deliver the ~$17bn Q4 and keep Data Center growth accelerating.
Cash flow and inventory: free cash flow fell sharply as inventory built up.
Gaming weakness and the small dip in gross margin guided for Q4 (55% vs 56%).
